:::{#thm-kolmogorov-invariance}
#### The choice of computer changes $\kolm$ by at most a constant

Let $\kolm_U$ and $\kolm_A$ be the
[Kolmogorov complexities](#def-kolmogorov-complexity)
and [conditional Kolmogorov complexities](#def-conditional-kolmogorov-complexity)
defined with universal computers $U$ and $A$.
There is a constant $c_A$, which depends on $U$ and $A$ but not on $x$ or $n$,
such that

$$\kolm_U\paren{x} \le \kolm_A\paren{x} + c_A
\quad \text{and} \quad
\kolm_U\paren{x \mid n} \le \kolm_A\paren{x \mid n} + c_A$$

for every binary string $x$ and every integer $n$.

:::

::: {.proof}
Because $U$ is universal, some program $s_A$ makes $U$ simulate $A$:
given $s_A$ followed by a program $p$ for $A$,
$U$ outputs whatever $A$ outputs on $p$.
So if $p$ is a shortest program for $x$ on $A$,
then $s_A$ followed by $p$ is a program for $x$ on $U$, and
$\kolm_U\paren{x} \le \strlen{s_A} + \strlen{p} = \kolm_A\paren{x} + \strlen{s_A}$.
The same program $s_A$ also passes $n$ on to $A$,
which gives the conditional bound in the same way.
Take $c_A = \strlen{s_A}$.
@cover2006elements [section 14.2] give this argument in full.

:::
